turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You may play with Estella, she is a suitable companion for a boy of your age.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am very sorry, Miss Havisham, but I am not in a position to play.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I do not understand what you mean by 'not in a position to play'. You are a boy, are you not?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, but I have to go home soon.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And what is it to you where you go or when you go?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It is because my sister is ill and needs me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I do not care about your sister's illness, Pip. I care about your company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid I must go, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You shall not go, Pip. You shall play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I do not want to be a bother, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are not a bother, Pip. You are a distraction.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am afraid I must insist, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You shall do as I say, Pip. You shall play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I do not think I can, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, Pip. I will not be disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I am very sorry, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You should be sorry, Pip. You are a disobedient boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will go, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will stay, Pip. You will play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will not stay, Miss Havisham.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy and had come to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer and let her look at him.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not afraid.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched when she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he knew it was her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that her heart was broken.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired and wanted diversion.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies and had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham repeatedly told Pip to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not sullen and obstinate, but was very sorry for Miss Havisham and could not play just now.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham ordered Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella, who was at the door.
